newsitem.title: FINLAND: Fuel added FIM 60 mln to Finnair H1 costs.
newsitem.headline: Fuel added FIM 60 mln to Finnair H1 costs.

text.p: Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy said on Friday surging fuel prices added 60 million markka to its costs in the first half of fiscal 1996/97.

"The cost of aircraft fuel during the first half was on average 22 percent higher than last year. This brought extra costs of 60 million markka compared with last year," Finnair said in a statement with its April-September results.
Finnair said its profit had been hit mainly by a slowdown in the growth of international scheduled flights, as well as the increase in costs, which it described as significant.

In the first half of 1996, it said there had been an about-face in Finnish air traffic as growth in international scheduled flight traffic came "almost to a standstill" while domestic traffic and chartered flights picked up clearly.
Finnair said earlier this week it was hiking fares to help offset higher fuel costs.
